content.user_title: Optimize Cloud Costs Across AWS, Azure, and GCP
content.value_statement: Cloud teams often overspend on idle, oversized, or poorly governed resources. This skill guides practical cost reviews, pricing choices, tagging, alerts, and architecture changes.
actual_capabilities: Explains visibility, right-sizing, pricing, and architecture optimization steps.
Compares AWS Reserved Instances, Savings Plans, Spot Instances, and S3 lifecycle policies.
Summarizes Azure Reserved VM Instances, Hybrid Benefit, Advisor, and storage optimization options.
Summarizes GCP committed use, sustained use, and preemptible VM options.
Provides Terraform-style examples for S3 lifecycle, tagging, budgets, and autoscaling.
Offers a cost optimization checklist and tool list for recurring reviews.
limitations: It does not connect to live cloud accounts or billing APIs.
Savings percentages are general guidance and may differ by region, contract, and current provider pricing.
Terraform examples require review and testing before use in production.
Referenced playbook, tagging guide, and spreadsheet files are not included in the scanned package.

use_cases.title: Reduce Monthly Cloud Spend
use_cases.description: Identify idle resources, oversized instances, storage lifecycle options, and pricing commitments for a focused savings review.

use_cases.title: Create FinOps Governance
use_cases.description: Define tagging standards, budget alerts, ownership signals, anomaly detection, and recurring cost review practices.

use_cases.title: Plan Multi-Cloud Optimization
use_cases.description: Compare AWS, Azure, and GCP cost levers before changing workload placement or commitment strategy.

prompt_templates.title: Review Cloud Spend Basics
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to review my cloud cost problem. I use [provider], and my goals are [goals]. Start with a simple checklist.

prompt_templates.title: Right-Size Resources
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to identify right-sizing opportunities for these resources: [resources]. Consider utilization, reliability needs, and rollback steps.

prompt_templates.title: Design Cost Governance
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to design tagging, budget alerts, anomaly detection, and review routines for [team or account scope]. Include owners and verification.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Multi-Cloud Savings
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to compare committed discounts, storage lifecycle options, and architecture changes across AWS, Azure, and GCP for [workload]. Include risks and validation steps.

output_examples.input: A team wants to reduce storage costs without losing compliance data.
output: Classify hot, warm, cold, and archive data by retention need.
Move older objects to lower-cost storage classes after validation.
Set budget alerts and review lifecycle changes monthly.

output_examples.input: A platform team needs a cost governance plan for three product groups.
output_examples.output: The response defines required tags, budget owners, alert thresholds, dashboard metrics, and a weekly review cadence.

output_examples.input: An engineering lead is planning savings commitments for stable workloads.
output_examples.output: The response compares reserved capacity, savings plans, committed use discounts, spot usage, and rollback limits.

best_practices: Validate every change with current billing data and workload metrics.
Pair cost reductions with reliability, compliance, and rollback requirements.
Use tags and alerts before making large pricing commitments.
anti_patterns: Buying long-term commitments before confirming steady baseline usage.
Deleting resources only because they look idle, without owner review.
Applying one provider strategy across all clouds without checking service rules.

faq.question: Does this skill connect to cloud accounts?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and examples, but it does not access billing systems or live infrastructure.

faq.question: Which providers does it cover?
faq.answer: It covers AWS, Azure, and GCP cost optimization themes and selected service examples.

faq.question: Can it produce Terraform changes?
faq.answer: It includes Terraform-style examples. Generated changes still need review, testing, and provider documentation checks.

faq.question: Is it suitable for FinOps planning?
faq.answer: Yes. It supports tagging, budgets, anomaly detection, commitments, and recurring cost reviews.

faq.question: Does it guarantee savings percentages?
faq.answer: No. Savings depend on pricing, region, workload shape, contracts, and operational constraints.

faq.question: What information should I provide?
faq.answer: Provide provider, services, monthly spend, utilization metrics, constraints, and reliability requirements.
